feedback.answered: Source observation: hup refuses to campaign while a committed configuration change lies above reported applied; candidates receiving append/heartbeat/snapshot become followers, so ordinary received commitment cannot silently install a new prefix while preserving candidacy. Existing tests expect the campaign and transfer guard, but those tests are not new execution evidence. Inference under faithful completed-application reporting: delayed old-term configuration changes block becoming leader, while configuration committed by the current leader normally follows a current-term commit that already releases pending reads. Contrary interface evidence prevents general closure: Node.Advance explicitly permits finishing Ready before command application completes, and doc.go allows Advance at any point after persistence with application order preserved. Node.run -> RawNode.Advance -> MsgStorageApplyResp advances the reported applied index used by the guard. Therefore the missing release call must be assessed against this entry-specific scheduling permission, not only the guard. Async storage responses have a different completed-work contract.

feedback.rationale: Next use a small clean-copy exploration with the public Node API, actual produced messages and FIFO application batches. It will test the limiting legal-history premise before spending an obligation on an unproven liveness interpretation. A four-to-three voter reduction changes threshold from three to two; preserving a delayed application batch while allowing only two replicas to append the new-term entry makes the config activation effect discriminating.
